stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x - 4)(x + 10)\). What is the minimum value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: The zeros of \(f\) are \(4\) and \(-10\). The vertex lies halfway between them, at \(x = \frac{4 + (-10)}{2} = -3\).
The parabola opens upward, so the minimum is \(f(-3) = (-3 - 4)(-3 + 10) = (-7)(7) = -49\).
verify:
x = symbols('x')
f = (x - 4)*(x + 10)
crit = solve(diff(f, x), x)
assert crit == [-3] and diff(f, x, 2) > 0
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [f.subs(x, -3)] == [-49]
